dispatch.ordering: Execute action before publishing a nonnegative next state. All entries in this table are ordinary transitions or empty entries, not completion function pointers. Notifications retain both action-time phase and pre-transition state.
ordinary_state_changes: initialize: 0 -> 1 only after actual socket task87 callback
deinitialize: 1 -> 0 only after actual socket task87 callback
stop: 6/7 -> 6 if selected service handles request; otherwise publish state3, request LAN stop, publish phase3
interface-result: 3 -> 1 with Stop(0); 4 -> 1 with Start(-255) before Reset(0)

completion_rules: Task86 initialization and deinitialization wait for real task87 completion, not queue admission. Their stock wait-flag callbacks ignore callback status.
StartLan and StopLan callbacks normalize failure to -255 and enqueue task86 messages660d and660e. Their primary table handlers branch on current state, not the status word.
Operation0/3/4 completion uses Operation registration; operation1 uses OperationReset; operation2 uses OperationDone. Completion clears the active operation before notification.
Completion6609 sets the completion flag before notifying; Event660a clears it before notifying. Both act only in state7.
The state6 default handler queues Stop only when the selected service does not handle the message and the stop-command guard permits admission.
Late messages use the current source transition table. LAN callback routing does not discard an older actual callback merely because a newer operation exists.
